case_studies.title: No Two Developers Think Alike: How Problem-Solving Styles and Experience Shape Needs in Conversational Interaction with Copilot
case_studies.abstract: Conversational LLM-based ``programming assistants'' provide a range of benefits to developers. However, recent studies demonstrate the variety in individual developers' needs regarding programming assistants, and challenges encountered by only specific groups of developers. In this study, we explore the role of cognitive diversity in shaping interactions with GitHub Copilot chat. Through a mixed-methods think aloud study with 27 professional developers and students, we characterize 5 distinct ``interaction modes'' and 10 underlying needs in developers' interactions, forming a conceptual model.
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of understanding how different developers interact with conversational programming assistants like GitHub Copilot. The study built a conceptual model of 5 interaction modes and 10 underlying needs. The result helps identify how developers with different problem-solving styles and experience levels use these assistants.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on how developers interact with programming assistants rather than cloud infrastructure management. If you oversee development teams using GitHub Copilot, you might find this research useful for understanding team dynamics. No immediate action is required for cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel study on developer interactions with LLM-based assistants shows potential for real-world IT relevance.

case_studies.title: PhantomSkill: Malicious Code Injection in Agent Skill Ecosystems
case_studies.abstract: Agent skills allow LLM-based coding agents to acquire domain-specific capabilities from third-party packages, but they also introduce a new supply-chain attack surface. We present PhantomSkill, an attack framework that hides malicious behavior in a skill's auxiliary resources rather than in its textual description. PhantomSkill uses a technique called VulMask to rewrite malicious scripts into vulnerability-shaped implementations. case_studies.title: Data Intelligence Agents: Interpreting, Modeling, and Querying Enterprise Data via Autonomous Coding Agents
case_studies.abstract: Production data integration is bottlenecked by repeated, lossy handoffs between data owners, engineers, and analysts who must collaboratively discover, structure, and query enterprise data. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of manual data integration by automating the process through autonomous coding agents. case_studies.title: Enhancing Decision-Making with Large Language Models through Multi-Agent Fictitious Play
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have demonstrated great potential in solving tasks with execution complexity, by distributing subtasks across cooperative agents. However, this divide-and-conquer paradigm falls short on decision-making tasks that are also prevalent in the real world. These tasks require simultaneous reasoning from the stances of all involved stakeholders whose decisions are mutually dependent and thus cannot be solved in isolation. We characterize this challenge as stance entanglement, a form of decision complexity distinct from execution complexity.
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of decision-making complexity in tasks that require simultaneous reasoning from multiple stakeholders, by building a large language model-based multi-agent system that uses fictitious play to make decisions. The result is an enhanced decision-making process that can handle tasks with mutually dependent decisions. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Structured Inference with Large Language Gibbs
case_studies.abstract: The knowledge encoded in large language models (LLMs) can serve as a substrate for structured reasoning over variables describing a complex world, but accessing this knowledge in a probabilistically coherent manner poses a difficult inference problem. We propose Large Language Gibbs, a scheme for structured probabilistic inference that uses conditional distributions of an LLM as transition operators. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of accessing knowledge in large language models in a probabilistically coherent manner by building a scheme called Large Language Gibbs, which uses conditional distributions of a large language model as transition operators, resulting in more accurate probabilistic inference. The scheme allows for iterative resampling of individual variables conditioned on others. This is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: PseudoBench: Measuring How Agentic Auto-Research Fuels Pseudoscience
case_studies.abstract: As Large Language Model based agents enter autonomous scientific research, their ability to resist pseudoscience becomes increasingly important. Otherwise, such systems may rapidly generate plausible yet misleading studies that contaminate academic literature and erode trust in science. We present PseudoBench, an adversarial benchmark for evaluating whether agentic auto-research systems can identify and resist pseudoscientific narratives. case_studies.title: Dango: A Strictly L1-Only Large Language Model for Studying Second Language Acquisition
case_studies.abstract: We introduce Dango, a 1.8B-parameter large language model designed for controlled studies of L1-to-L2 (Japanese-to-English) transfer in second language acquisition (SLA). While previous studies have explored SLA in language models, they have predominantly relied on smaller or non-decoder models, limiting their ability to generate open-ended text and reducing their suitability as practical L2 simulators. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of L2 contamination in large language models, introducing Dango, a 1.8B-parameter model for studying second language acquisition. The result is a more accurate and practical simulator for L2 acquisition. This is not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: CodeSentinel: A Three-Layer Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection in Code Contexts
case_studies.abstract: Code large language models increasingly retrieve external code context from repositories, documentation, issue threads, and coding-agent environments, creating an indirect prompt-injection surface where attackers hide instructions in comments, strings, identifiers, or decoy code. We propose CodeSentinel, a three-layer inference-time sanitizer. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of indirect prompt injection in code contexts by building a three-layer defense system called CodeSentinel, which detects and sanitizes malicious code. CodeSentinel uses a combination of techniques to identify and remove adversarial triggers in code comments, strings, and identifiers. The result is a more secure code environment for large language models.
